channel.title: Apple Core Updates
channel.description: Updates for Apple Core - a native macOS MCP server for Apple services

item.title: Version 1.0.8
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.8

Fixed

  • Calendar and Reminders tools now return the item's identifier. Previously events_fetch, events_create, reminders_fetch, and the other read/create tools returned objects with no id, so events_update, events_delete, reminders_update, reminders_delete, and reminders_complete — which all require an identifier — could not be used through the API. Events expose their eventIdentifier and reminders their calendarItemIdentifier (as the JSON-LD @id), matching how each tool resolves the item.
  • calendars_list and the reminder-list tool now include each calendar's identifier.

item.title: Version 1.0.7
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.7

Fixed

  • Enabling a service from the status menu no longer fails with "Apple Core could not become the active app". Activation is now re-requested while waiting and treated as best-effort, so the permission request itself always runs.
  • When macOS refuses to display a permission dialog (the request comes back denied but no decision is recorded), Calendar, Contacts, Reminders, and Capture now report that the prompt was suppressed instead of claiming access was denied. The message points at non-default security configurations — for example amfi_get_out_of_my_way in boot-args, which marks every third-party process as a platform binary and causes macOS 26 (Tahoe) to deny consent prompts outright.

Notes

  • If a Mac's toggles fail with the new "macOS refused to display the permission request" message, no in-app change can help: restore the default security configuration (clear the custom boot-args, re-enable SIP) or grant access by other means, then try again.

item.title: Version 1.0.6
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.6

Apple Core 1.0.6 makes macOS privacy prompts work from both the menu bar and Settings on a Mac with no existing grants.

Fixes

  • Apple Core now becomes a regular foreground app and waits for macOS to confirm that it is active before requesting access. Earlier builds called the permission API immediately after asking to become active, and Tahoe could deny that request without displaying a prompt.
  • Calendar, Contacts, and Reminders now check the result of the permission request. A denied request can no longer leave the service checked and available to the MCP server.
  • Mail and Notes now request their Automation grants when you enable the service. Messages requests Automation before guiding you through access to chat.db.
  • Capture requests Camera, Microphone, and Screen Recording access even if one of the other grants is denied.
  • The menu bar and Settings now update the server only after activation finishes. If macOS denies access, the switch returns to off and the server keeps the service unavailable.

Permission coverage

Calendar, Contacts, Location, and Reminders use their native macOS permission prompts. Maps uses the Location grant. Mail and Notes use Automation, while Messages uses Automation plus the existing database picker. Capture uses Camera, Microphone, and Screen Recording.

Shortcuts and Utilities do not need a macOS privacy grant, so they enable without a permission prompt.

Upgrading

1.0.3 and later update automatically. Installs on 1.0.0 through 1.0.2 still need the one-time manual reinstall described in the 1.0.3 notes, because their update signing key no longer matches the feed.

item.title: Version 1.0.5
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.5

Apple Core 1.0.5 makes /favicon.ico serve a real icon file, so clients that read connector branding from the origin can actually decode it.

Fixes

  • /favicon.ico returns a real ICO container: the route answered with a bare 32x32 PNG body labelled image/png. The path claims an ICO container and the content type disagreed with both the path and the bytes, which strict icon resolvers reject outright. The rendered PNG is now wrapped in a genuine single-entry ICO and served as image/x-icon. Every other favicon size is unchanged.
  • The landing page advertises fewer, smaller icons: it listed all seven PNG sizes, which put a 256x256 image ahead of anything cheap. Icon resolvers take the first usable declaration, so the page now offers the ICO plus the 16 and 32 pixel PNGs. All sizes remain served for clients that request them directly.

Notes

These routes stay unauthenticated and unconditional, so pointing your own Cloudflare Tunnel at Apple Core vends the Apple Core logo from your own domain with no extra configuration.

If your MCP client still shows a different icon after updating, the cause is likely outside Apple Core: some clients resolve a connector's icon at the registrable domain rather than the exact hostname, so a subdomain's own favicon may never be requested.

Upgrading

1.0.3 and later update automatically. Installs on 1.0.0 through 1.0.2 still need the one-time manual reinstall described in the 1.0.3 notes, because their update signing key no longer matches the feed.

item.title: Version 1.0.4
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.4

Apple Core 1.0.4 fixes remote OAuth discovery and stops service toggles from failing silently.

Fixes

  • Cloud connectors can complete OAuth: the OAuth issuer and the allowed-origin list are now both derived from the tunnel hostname. A server first configured without a hostname kept a localhost-only origin list and went on advertising an issuer of http://localhost:8756 through the public tunnel, so any cloud client that read the discovery documents was sent to the user's own machine and could never finish the flow. A config written before the hostname existed now repairs itself at launch instead of only when the Cloudflare pane is opened.
  • Service toggles explain themselves: a toggle that could not be enabled reverted with no message, which was indistinguishable from a broken control. The row now shows what macOS refused.
  • Refused permission prompts are named as such: macOS reports a plain "denied" both when you click Don't Allow and when it declines to show a prompt at all. The second case is the normal one on a Mac reached over Screen Sharing, where another process holds the foreground, tccd logs "Policy disallows prompt", and nothing is written to the privacy database — so no service can ever be granted there. Apple Core now distinguishes the two and says which happened.

Upgrading

1.0.3 and later update automatically. Installs on 1.0.0 through 1.0.2 still need the one-time manual reinstall described in the 1.0.3 notes, because their update signing key no longer matches the feed.

item.title: Version 1.0.3
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.3

Apple Core 1.0.3 repairs automatic updates and rebuilds Cloudflare Tunnel setup around a guided flow.

Update this release manually

The update signing key has changed. Builds from 1.0.0 through 1.0.2 carry a public key whose private half is no longer available, so they cannot validate the update feed and show "The update feed is improperly signed and could not be validated." Download 1.0.3 from Releases and replace the app once. Automatic updates work normally from 1.0.3 onward.

Earlier notes claimed this was fixed in 1.0.1. That was wrong: the feed was well-formed, but it was signed with a different key than the one shipped in the app, so no release could ever verify it.

Fixes

  • Hostnames with a scheme or path are accepted: pasting https://mcp.example.com/mcp into the Cloudflare Hostname field now reduces to mcp.example.com. Previously the whole string went to cloudflared tunnel route dns, which rejected it as an invalid hostname, and the failure appeared only in the log.
  • Routing failures are visible: a DNS route that cannot be created is reported in the Cloudflare pane instead of being discarded. A tunnel that starts without routing anywhere is no longer reported as a success.
  • Tunnel status tells the truth: the pane no longer shows "Cloudflare tunnel started" beside a Stopped badge. Loading the LaunchAgent is now confirmed to have produced a running process before the app claims it started.

Cloudflare setup

  • A Before You Start checklist shows whether cloudflared is installed and whether you are signed in to Cloudflare, with the exact command or button to fix each.
  • Log In to Cloudflare runs the browser sign-in from inside the app. Apple Core detects the resulting account certificate rather than failing later with an opaque error.
  • Set Up & Start replaces Start Tunnel as the primary action, and runs the whole sequence: find or create the named tunnel, route the hostname in DNS, write the config and LaunchAgent, then start. Start Tunnel skipped DNS routing and now lives in Tunnel Actions as "Start Tunnel Only".
  • Every field explains itself, and the Hostname field shows inline why a value cannot be routed.

item.title: Version 1.0.2
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.2

Apple Core 1.0.2 fixes three issues that affected new-machine setup and adds control over the Dock icon.

Fixes

  • Duplicate menu bar items: the LaunchAgent now launches the app through open -W via LaunchServices instead of running the bare executable directly. LaunchServices deduplicates instances, so the LaunchAgent and a manual app open no longer produce two menu bar icons.
  • Service toggles not working on a new computer: the app now fronts itself before requesting macOS privacy permissions. Without this, TCC silently denied permission requests from a background-only accessory app with no visible prompt, so toggling Calendar, Contacts, Reminders, or other services did nothing.
  • Sparkle update feed error: the signed appcast was already corrected in 1.0.1; this release confirms the fix by shipping with the corrected feed configuration.

New

  • Show Dock Icon toggle: Apple Core is now a menu-bar-only app by default (no Dock icon). A new toggle in Settings > Server > General lets you opt into showing the Dock icon when the app is running.

item.title: Version 1.0.1
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0.1

Apple Core 1.0.1 keeps remote MCP clients signed in after their 12-hour access token expires.

OAuth refresh tokens

  • OAuth clients now receive a refresh token with each access token. Apple Core rotates the refresh token every time it is used.
  • Refresh tokens are bound to the client and MCP resource that received them. A token cannot be reused after rotation.
  • Existing token files remain readable. Connections created before this release need one new sign-in because their saved records do not contain a refresh token.

This release also adds direct tests for refresh-token rotation, persistence, client and resource binding, and private token-file permissions.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
Apple Core 1.0

Apple Core is a native macOS menu bar app that lets MCP clients work with Apple services on your Mac. The standard build has 77 tools for Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, Location, Maps, Messages, screen and camera capture, Shortcuts, Notes, Mail, and utility tasks.

Connections use a bearer token that the app generates locally. New installs listen only on localhost. Remote access is optional, and each service stays local until you turn on its Remote toggle. If you choose to use a Cloudflare Tunnel, Apple Core creates configuration for your own Cloudflare account.

The download does not contain the developer's bearer token, Cloudflare credentials, OAuth clients, Apple account data, or macOS privacy permissions. Every Mac starts with its own configuration under ~/.config/apple-core/ and requests access to Apple services through the normal macOS permission controls.

Version 1.0 is signed with a Developer ID certificate, notarized by Apple, and distributed through a signed Sparkle update feed.
